title: Platform Control Plane (Backstage App Factory)
tagline: Backstage control plane that generates React apps from one template, with a shared UI package and an SDK whose adapters fail closed.
summary: A Backstage-based control plane and App Factory for a shared frontend standard. A scaffolder template generates a React 19, Vite and TypeScript app that vendors two packages: @platform/ui (tokens, accessible primitives, a Storybook design-system portal) and @platform/sdk (app identity, runtime mode, navigation, auth, permissions and tenant adapters). The README is in Thai. docs/status.md lists what is supported and what is not shipped, such as a tenant backend and an identity-provider service.

claims.text: The repo is a Backstage control plane with an App Factory scaffolder template plus two shared packages, @platform/ui and @platform/sdk. The README says the control plane is not a product's runtime, and docs/status.md says the repository does not generate a business backend.

The SDK's standalone adapters fail closed: sign-in and sign-out reject with PlatformCapabilityUnavailableError, and permissions and tenant return no snapshot, which status.md says makes can() return false. resolvePlatformRuntime picks standalone or hosted from the app's mode and throws when a platform-mfe app has no host.

docs/status.md separates 'supported and verified' items from integration boundaries and unshipped work, listing a tenant backend among the unshipped items. CI runs lint, typecheck, the portal build, tests, the build and compose validation, then an e2e job; no CI output is stored in the repo.
Repository facts from a git run: 30 commits, all under the owner's account, between 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-21, and 6 ADR files under docs/adr.

excerpts.title: Standalone adapters report 'unavailable' instead of faking a capability
excerpts.why: The comment says auth, permissions and tenant are capabilities this phase deliberately does not implement. Sign-in and sign-out reject with a typed error, and permissions and tenant return a null snapshot, so a generated app without a provider cannot appear signed in or authorised.

excerpts.title: One function gives the scaffold-time mode a runtime meaning
excerpts.why: standalone ignores any host, platform-mfe requires one and throws otherwise, and standalone-and-mfe uses a host only if present. The default branch throws on an unknown mode because platform-app.json can be edited by hand.

demo.note: Runs locally (Backstage backend and app dev servers, plus a Storybook design-system portal); no public deployment is documented.

limitations: docs/status.md says what is not shipped: a platform-owned identity-provider service or enterprise SSO deployment, tenant backend and resource-scoped authorization, provider and backend services behind the feature packs (profile, dashboard, settings, report, history and audit persistence), and a Super App host runtime with Module Federation loading (E6, E7). tenant, desktop-ready and mobile-ready are recorded-only selections (E16).
'Supported and verified' in docs/status.md (E12) is the repo's own statement. No test, CI or e2e output is stored in the repo, and nothing was run here except the git facts in the capture.
status.md calls itself more authoritative than older phase reports (E13); the ADRs and BACKSTAGE_APP_FACTORY_PHASE reports are historical records and may not describe current behaviour.
App Factory publishing needs a GitHub token supplied by the operator (per the README); this entry did not exercise it.
The README is in Thai and embeds a screenshot from a local run; no images are shown here.
contribution: All 30 commits are attributed to the owner's account, 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-21 (see capture platform-control-plane-git-facts). No other contributors.
